trials.name: BioFINDER2
trials.population: Cognitively healthy individuals, subjective cognitive decline, MCI, AD dementia, and other dementias.
trials.primary_endpoint: Clinical diagnosis according to consensus group decision and change in Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB).
trials.results_summary: As a longitudinal biomarker cohort, BioFINDER-2 has not completed its final readout but has produced numerous publications showing the utility of tau-PET, p-tau, and other biomarkers in predicting AD progression.

trials.name: ADNI3
trials.population: Cognitively normal, mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and mild AD dementia participants.
trials.primary_endpoint: Rate of change in cognition as measured by ADAS-Cog13, Logical Memory Test, and MMSE over 5 years.
trials.results_summary: Longitudinal data from ADNI3 provided validation for the predictive models developed in BioFINDER-2, confirming that tau-PET and baseline cognition strongly predict cognitive decline.

trials.name: TRAILBLAZER-ALZ
trials.population: Participants with early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease enrolled specifically based on tau-PET imaging (intermediate tau pathology).
trials.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline in the Integrated Alzheimer's Disease Rating Scale (iADRS) Score at 76 Weeks.
trials.results_summary: The trial successfully demonstrated that donanemab slowed cognitive and functional decline at 76 weeks compared to placebo. It effectively validated the tau-PET enrichment strategy theoretically proposed in the document.

trials.name: TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2
trials.population: Participants with early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease (MCI or mild dementia) with tau-PET evidence of AD pathology.
trials.primary_endpoint: Change From Baseline on the Integrated Alzheimer's Disease Rating Scale (iADRS) at Week 76.
trials.results_summary: Confirmed the Phase 2 findings, showing donanemab significantly slowed clinical decline (iADRS and CDR-SB) at 76 weeks in early AD patients enriched for tau pathology, leading to FDA approval.

related_evidence.description: NEJM publication of TRAILBLAZER-ALZ (Phase 2 donanemab) results validating tau-PET enrichment.
JAMA publication of TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 (Phase 3 donanemab) results confirming the efficacy of drug in a tau-PET enriched cohort.
FDA approves donanemab (Kisunla) for early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease based on the TRAILBLAZER-ALZ trials.

evidence_assessment: The document claims that tau-PET imaging combined with baseline cognition offers superior prediction of cognitive decline compared to fluid biomarkers (like p-tau), enabling powerful clinical trial enrichment. This theoretical finding is strongly supported by real-world clinical trial data, most notably Eli Lilly's donanemab program. The Phase 2 (TRAILBLAZER-ALZ) and Phase 3 (TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2) trials utilized tau-PET to enroll patients with intermediate tau pathology, effectively validating that such enrichment strategies yield cohorts with predictable clinical trajectories. This allowed the drug's disease-modifying effects to be robustly proven, leading to the FDA approval of donanemab (Kisunla) in July 2024. Overall, the clinical evidence overwhelmingly validates the document's central assertion that biomarker-based enrichment using tau-PET significantly optimizes interventional AD trials.
